Currently, LinkedIn's web crawler (`LinkedInBot`) is scraping a few text strings from our country landing pages and automatically posting them to our LinkedIn Company Page as "Basic Jobs." We want to scale this up intentionally. We need to build dynamic, crawler-friendly job detail pages for all 500+ roles in our database, inject the correct `schema.org/JobPosting` JSON-LD so LinkedIn and Google Jobs scrape them, and design an interstitial landing page that captures the inbound traffic from LinkedIn before they bounce to the external employer. ### Technical Requirements #### 1. Dynamic Job Routes (SSR or SSG) Create a new dynamic route for individual job postings: `/jobs/[slug]` (e.g., `/jobs/flixbus-senior-backend-engineer`). * **Crawler Friendly:** This page *must* be Server-Side Rendered (SSR) or Statically Generated (SSG/ISR). Bots like `LinkedInBot` and `Googlebot` will not execute complex client-side JavaScript or authenticate to view this page. The raw HTML must contain the job data on the first load. #### 2. Schema.org / JSON-LD Injection (Crucial for LinkedIn) In the `` of the `/jobs/[slug]` route, inject a strictly formatted `schema.org/JobPosting` JSON-LD script. * **The "Hiring Organization" Hack:** To ensure LinkedIn maps this job to the **Kuchup** LinkedIn Company Page (and not the external employer's page), the `hiringOrganization` must be set to Kuchup. We will clarify the actual employer in the job title and description. **Implement this exact JSON-LD structure:** ```json { "@context": "https://schema.org/", "@type": "JobPosting", "title": "{job.title} at {job.external_company_name} (Visa Sponsorship)", "description": "{job.html_description}

Note: This role is curated by Kuchup. Apply via our workspace to track your application and tailor your CV.", "identifier": { "@type": "PropertyValue", "name": "Kuchup", "value": "{job.internal_id}" }, "datePosted": "{job.created_at_iso_format}", "validThrough": "{job.expiration_date_iso_format}", "employmentType": "{job.employment_type}", "hiringOrganization": { "@type": "Organization", "name": "Kuchup", "sameAs": "https://kuchup.com", "logo": "https://kuchup.com/logo.png" }, "jobLocation": { "@type": "Place", "address": { "@type": "PostalAddress", "addressLocality": "{job.city}", "addressCountry": "{job.country_code}" } }, "applyUrl": "https://kuchup.com/jobs/{job.slug}" } ``` #### 3. Interstitial Landing Page UX (Traffic Capture) When a user clicks "Apply" on the LinkedIn job post, they will be sent to `[https://kuchup.com/jobs/](https://kuchup.com/jobs/)[slug]`. **Do not automatically redirect them to the external employer.** We must capture this traffic. Build the UI for `/jobs/[slug]` with the following hierarchy: * **Header:** Job Title, Actual Employer (e.g., FlixBus), Location, and a prominent "Visa Sponsorship Supported" badge. * **Body:** The job description. * **Call to Action Box (Sticky or Prominent):** * **Primary Button (High Contrast):** "Track & Prepare Application via Kuchup" -> (Redirects to auth/signup, then drops them into the personalized workspace with this job saved and the Claude/Cursor MCP instructions ready). * **Secondary Button (Subtle/Text-link):** "Continue to official {employer} career page" -> (Standard `target="_blank"` link to the ATS, passing through analytics tracking). * **Value Prop block:** Briefly explain what Kuchup is to cold traffic: *"Kuchup is a workspace for international engineers. Track your relocation roles and tailor your CV with our Claude/Cursor MCP integration."* #### 4. XML Sitemap & Robots.txt To ensure `LinkedInBot` and `Googlebot` find all 500+ jobs instantly: 1. Create a dynamic route `/server-sitemap-jobs.xml` (or similar depending on the framework). 2. Query the database for all *active* jobs and generate standard XML sitemap `` nodes pointing to `/jobs/[slug]`. 3. Add a `` tag based on when the job was added/updated. 4. Update the root `/robots.txt` to include: `Sitemap: [https://kuchup.com/server-sitemap-jobs.xml](https://kuchup.com/server-sitemap-jobs.xml)`. #### 5. Expiration / Cleanup Logic When a job is no longer active (removed from the employer's ATS in your 6-hour refresh cycle): * Remove it from the `sitemap.xml`. * Change the `/jobs/[slug]` route to return a **410 Gone** HTTP status (preferred over 404), or render a UI that says "This role has been closed" with a button to "Browse similar relocation roles in {job.country}". --- ### Next steps for the Agent: Please confirm you understand this architecture. Start by scaffolding the dynamic `/jobs/[slug]` route and the JSON-LD injection logic based on our current frontend framework.

# Job wrapping / syndication funnel

## Architecture (locked)

The public homepage is Next.js with `output: "export"` ([homepage/next.config.ts](homepage/next.config.ts)), copied into Flask as static HTML. That cannot SSR 500+ DB-backed URLs that change every 6 hours, nor return **410 Gone**.

**Job pages live in Flask**, next to the existing SEO surface (`/robots.txt`, `/sitemap.xml` in [relocation_jobs/web/server.py](relocation_jobs/web/server.py)). Next.js stays the marketing site (country guides, pricing, MCP). Job HTML uses the same design tokens ([relocation_jobs/static/design-tokens.css](relocation_jobs/static/design-tokens.css)) so the interstitial looks like kuchup.com.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  LinkedInBot --> JobPage
  Googlebot --> Sitemap
  Sitemap --> JobPage
  User["LinkedIn Apply click"] --> JobPage
  JobPage["Flask GET /jobs/slug"] --> Postgres
  JobPage --> Primary["Google OAuth next=/jobs/slug/save"]
  JobPage --> Secondary["Tracked outbound to ATS"]
  Primary --> Workspace["Company workspace + looking-to-apply"]
  Workspace --> Credits["Free quota then credit packs"]
```

This is also the conversion design: **do not auto-redirect to the employer**. The page is the product. Primary CTA creates a Free account (30 monthly credits, 20 MCP writes/day) and saves the role. Money happens later when they hit board/MCP walls — same model as [docs/reference/entitlements-and-opportunities.md](docs/reference/entitlements-and-opportunities.md).

## What we do not have today

`matching_jobs` has `id`, `title`, `url`, `description_text`, `location`, `fetched`, `last_seen`, `visa_sponsorship`. It does **not** have `public_slug`, `employment_type`, or `expiration_date`. Stale ATS rows are **kept**, not deleted ([relocation_jobs/scrape/merge.py](relocation_jobs/scrape/merge.py) `stale_kept`; repo only deletes keys missing from the merged in-memory board).

JSON-LD fields we will derive, not invent columns for:

- `employmentType` → `FULL_TIME` unless we later scrape it
- `datePosted` → `fetched` / `last_seen` as ISO date
- `validThrough` → `datePosted + 30 days` while open; `closed_at` when closed
- `addressCountry` → ISO from company country key (`germany`→`DE`, `uk`→`GB`, …)
- `addressLocality` → job `location` / company `city`
- `logo` → existing `https://kuchup.com/static/icons/kuchup-bird.png`, plus a `/logo.png` alias so the requested JSON-LD URL resolves

**Syndication set:** visa-positive jobs only. The specified title always includes `(Visa Sponsorship)`. Putting unknown/negative-visa roles in that schema would be false advertising and would burn LinkedIn/Google trust.

**Closed jobs:** add `closed_at` on `matching_jobs`. Set it on the stale-kept path during merge; clear it when the role reappears. Do not hard-delete — we need the row for 410 + “browse similar roles in {country}”.

## Data + slug

Migration (via existing [relocation_jobs/catalog/schema.py](relocation_jobs/catalog/schema.py) `run_migration_once`):

- `public_slug TEXT UNIQUE`
- `closed_at TEXT` (same date style as `fetched` / `last_seen`)

Slug: `slug_from_name(company) + "-" + slug_from_name(title)`, persist on first insert, never regenerate (stable LinkedIn URLs). Collision: append `-{id}`. Backfill existing visa-positive rows in the same migration/helper.

Repo (SQL stays in [relocation_jobs/catalog/repo.py](relocation_jobs/catalog/repo.py)):

- `get_public_job_by_slug(slug)` — join company; include closed rows
- `list_active_public_job_sitemap_entries()` — `visa_sponsorship = 1 AND closed_at IS NULL`

JSON-LD builder in catalog service (no SQL): exact structure you specified, plus schema.org `url` (Google uses `url`; `applyUrl` is the LinkedIn-oriented extra). Description = sanitized HTML from `format_job_description` ([relocation_jobs/scrape/descriptions.py](relocation_jobs/scrape/descriptions.py)) plus the Kuchup note.

`hiringOrganization.name = "Kuchup"` is implemented as specified so LinkedIn attaches to the company page. Title/description still name the real employer. Google Jobs may ignore or downrank mis-attributed `hiringOrganization`; LinkedIn wrapping is the commercial target.

## Flask routes

Register **before** the catch-all `/<path:slug>` in [relocation_jobs/web/server.py](relocation_jobs/web/server.py) (or in [relocation_jobs/web/routes/public.py](relocation_jobs/web/routes/public.py) — Flask specificity is enough if `/jobs/<slug>` is explicit).

| Route | Behavior |
|-------|----------|
| `GET /jobs/<slug>` | SSR Jinja. Open job: 200 + JSON-LD in `<head>`. Closed: **410** + “This role has been closed” + link to `/relocation-jobs-{country}`. Unknown slug: 404. |
| `GET /jobs/<slug>/save` | Auth required. `set_job_looking_to_apply` (free; does not spend a credit), then redirect to `/company/{country}/{company_slug}`. Unauthenticated → `/api/auth/google?next=/jobs/{slug}/save`. |
| `GET /jobs/<slug>/employer` | Log outbound click, 302 to ATS URL (analytics without relying on `target=_blank` beacons). |
| `GET /logo.png` | Alias to the bird PNG. |
| `GET /sitemap-jobs.xml` | Active visa jobs, `<loc>` + `<lastmod>` from `last_seen`/`fetched`. |
| `GET /robots.txt` | Keep `/sitemap.xml`; add `Sitemap: https://kuchup.com/sitemap-jobs.xml`. |

Jinja template: [relocation_jobs/web/templates/job_posting.html](relocation_jobs/web/templates/job_posting.html) (new). Flask already defaults templates next to `web/`. No Next.js job route.

Cache: short public cache (`max-age=300, stale-while-revalidate`) on 200; `no-store` on 410.

## Interstitial UX (conversion)

Do not send cold traffic to `/pricing` first. Give the aha moment, then the paywall.

- **Header:** title, real employer, location, visa-sponsorship badge (only if `visa_sponsorship` is true).
- **Body:** sanitized description HTML.
- **CTA box (sticky on desktop):**
  - Primary: “Track & prepare this application in Kuchup” → `/api/auth/google?next=/jobs/{slug}/save` (already signed-in: `/jobs/{slug}/save`).
  - Secondary (text link): “Continue to the official {employer} career page” → `/jobs/{slug}/employer`.
- **Value prop:** workspace for international engineers; track this role; tailor the CV with Claude/Cursor MCP. Free includes 30 credits/month and 20 MCP writes/day; credit packs when they need more matched roles.

Slim Flask header/footer (logo, country guides, Sign in) — do not try to import React Header.

## Tests and docs

- [tests/web/test_public_api.py](tests/web/test_public_api.py): robots extra sitemap line; jobs sitemap only active visa slugs; job page HTML contains JSON-LD + no auto-redirect; closed → 410; unknown → 404; `/save` unauthenticated redirects to Google with `next`.
- Catalog tests: slug uniqueness, `closed_at` set/cleared on merge.
- Update [docs/operations/seo-indexing.md](docs/operations/seo-indexing.md) — job URLs are now public; submit `/sitemap-jobs.xml` in Search Console. No live IPs/secrets.

## Implementation order

First ship crawlable HTML + JSON-LD (LinkedInBot). Then CTA/save. Then sitemap/410. UI uses existing tokens; no homepage rebuild required for job pages.

# SEO indexing

How to get kuchup.com found on Google and how LinkedIn discovers public job pages.

## Prerequisites

- Domain `kuchup.com` is live and serving the public homepage
- Preferred host is **apex** `https://kuchup.com` (`www` must 301 to apex)
- `robots.txt` at `https://kuchup.com/robots.txt` allows indexing
- `sitemap.xml` at `https://kuchup.com/sitemap.xml` is up to date (includes `<lastmod>`)
- `sitemap-jobs.xml` at `https://kuchup.com/sitemap-jobs.xml` lists active visa-sponsored `/jobs/<slug>` URLs
- Marketing pages deployed (see [ec2-panel.md](ec2-panel.md))

## After an SEO / marketing deploy

1. Confirm host consolidation:
   - `curl -sI https://www.kuchup.com/` → `301` with `Location: https://kuchup.com/...`
2. Spot-check head tags on `/` and one country page:
   - `rel="canonical"` points at apex
   - `og:image` absolute URL returns 200
   - `/favicon.ico` returns 200
3. Confirm marketing HTML is cacheable (`Cache-Control` is not `no-store` on `/`)
4. Re-submit `https://kuchup.com/sitemap.xml` and `https://kuchup.com/sitemap-jobs.xml` in Google Search Console
5. Request indexing for key URLs (URL inspection)
6. Spot-check a live job URL: `curl -s https://kuchup.com/jobs/<slug> | grep JobPosting` — JSON-LD must be in the first HTML response (no login wall)

## Google Search Console setup

1. Go to <https://search.google.com/search-console>
2. Add property: **URL prefix** `https://kuchup.com` (apex only after www redirects)
3. Verify ownership — choose any method:
   - **DNS TXT record** (recommended): add the TXT record in your DNS provider (Cloudflare).
   - **HTML file**: Google provides a file; drop it into `relocation_jobs/static/` and re-deploy.
   - **Google Analytics / Google Tag Manager**: if already installed.
4. Once verified, submit the sitemaps:
   - Navigate to **Sitemaps** section
   - Enter `https://kuchup.com/sitemap.xml` and submit
   - Enter `https://kuchup.com/sitemap-jobs.xml` and submit
5. Request manual indexing for key pages:
   - **URL inspection** → paste root URL → **Request indexing**
   - Repeat for: `/how-it-works`, `/pricing`, `/mcp`, `/relocation-jobs-germany`, `/relocation-jobs-netherlands`, `/relocation-jobs-uk`, `/relocation-jobs-portugal`, `/relocation-jobs-ireland`

## Public job pages

Visa-positive catalog jobs are public at `/jobs/<slug>`. Each page is server-rendered HTML with `schema.org/JobPosting` JSON-LD so LinkedInBot and Googlebot can read the posting without JavaScript.

- Open roles: HTTP 200, listed in `/sitemap-jobs.xml`
- Closed roles (dropped from the employer ATS on a successful refresh): HTTP **410**, omitted from the jobs sitemap, with a link to the country marketing page
- Unknown slugs: HTTP 404

`hiringOrganization` is Kuchup so LinkedIn can attach the posting to the company page. The job title and description name the real employer.

## What to expect

| Timeline | Event |
|----------|-------|
| Hours–days | Homepage indexed |
| Days–weeks | Marketing pages indexed |
| Days–weeks | Individual `/jobs/<slug>` URLs crawled from `/sitemap-jobs.xml` |
| Weeks–months | Category queries start returning results |

> Google may treat `hiringOrganization` that is not the employer as low-quality for Google Jobs. LinkedIn company-page wrapping is the intended distribution channel.

## Monitoring

- Check Search Console **Performance** tab weekly for clicks and impressions
- Watch **Coverage** for indexing errors or sitemap issues
- Fix any `noindex` flags, unexpected 404s, or crawl errors promptly
- Closed roles should be **410**, not lingering 200s in the jobs sitemap

# Job wrapping / syndication funnel

**Last updated:** 2026-09-06

Public `/jobs/<slug>` pages so LinkedInBot and Googlebot can read visa-sponsored catalog roles as `schema.org/JobPosting`, and so a LinkedIn Apply click lands on Kuchup instead of bouncing to the employer ATS.

Related: [seo-indexing.md](../operations/seo-indexing.md) (Search Console, sitemaps), [catalog-pattern.md](catalog-pattern.md) (shared catalog vs per-user overlay), [entitlements-and-opportunities.md](entitlements-and-opportunities.md) (Free credits / MCP quota), [company-workspace.md](company-workspace.md) (where save lands), [mcp-application.md](mcp-application.md) (CV reframe after save).

---

## Why this exists

LinkedIn’s crawler already picked up a few strings from country marketing pages and posted them as Basic Jobs on the Kuchup company page. This funnel makes that intentional:

1. **Discover** — crawlers get raw HTML + JSON-LD (no JS, no login).
2. **Map to Kuchup** — `hiringOrganization` is Kuchup so LinkedIn attaches the posting to our company page, not the employer’s.
3. **Capture** — Apply goes to `https://kuchup.com/jobs/<slug>`. We do **not** auto-redirect to the ATS.
4. **Convert** — primary CTA creates a Free account, marks the role looking-to-apply, and opens the company workspace. Credit packs / MCP quota walls come later.

Country marketing pages (`/relocation-jobs-*`) stay in the Next.js static export. Job detail URLs cannot: they change every 6-hour fetch, need 410 when a role closes, and must read Postgres. Those pages are Flask SSR.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  LinkedInBot --> JobPage
  Googlebot --> Sitemap
  Sitemap --> JobPage
  User["LinkedIn Apply"] --> JobPage
  JobPage["Flask GET /jobs/slug"] --> Postgres
  JobPage --> Primary["Google OAuth next=/jobs/slug/save"]
  JobPage --> Secondary["Tracked outbound to ATS"]
  Primary --> Workspace["Company workspace + looking-to-apply"]
  Workspace --> Credits["Free quota then credit packs"]
```

---

## Public URLs

| Path | Status | Who |
|------|--------|-----|
| `GET /jobs/<slug>` | 200 open · **410** closed · 404 unknown | Crawlers + humans. JSON-LD only on 200. |
| `GET /jobs/<slug>/save` | 302 | Humans. Unauthenticated → Google OAuth with `next=`. Authenticated → looking-to-apply, then `/company/<country>/<company-slug>`. `X-Robots-Tag: noindex`. |
| `GET /jobs/<slug>/employer` | 302 | Humans. Logs `employer_outbound`, then redirects to the ATS URL. `noindex`. |
| `GET /sitemap-jobs.xml` | 200 | Crawlers. Visa-positive, not closed, slug present. |
| `GET /robots.txt` | 200 | Lists both `/sitemap.xml` and `/sitemap-jobs.xml`. |
| `GET /logo.png` | 200 | JSON-LD `hiringOrganization.logo`. Alias of the bird PNG. |

Cache: open job pages and the jobs sitemap use `public, max-age=300, stale-while-revalidate=86400`. Closed pages are `no-store`.

**Syndication set:** `visa_sponsorship = 1` only. The JSON-LD title always includes `(Visa Sponsorship)`. Unknown or negative-visa roles are not public listings.

---

## Data

Catalog columns on `matching_jobs` (migration `catalog_public_job_syndication_v1` in [`catalog/schema.py`](../../relocation_jobs/catalog/schema.py)):

| Column | Role |
|--------|------|
| `public_slug` | Stable URL key. Unique when non-empty. Set once, never rewritten when the title changes. Collision: `{base}-{id}`. |
| `closed_at` | Set when merge keeps a job that the latest scrape dropped (`stale_kept`). Cleared when the role reappears. Empty string = open. Rows are **not** hard-deleted. |

Slug shape: `slug_from_name(company) + "-" + slug_from_name(title)` ([`core/slug.py`](../../relocation_jobs/core/slug.py) `public_job_slug_base`). Example: FlixBus + Senior Backend Engineer → `flixbus-senior-backend-engineer`.

Visa-positive rows are backfilled on migrate. Later upserts assign a slug to any job missing one so a later visa-positive flip still gets a URL.

Merge behavior ([`scrape/merge.py`](../../relocation_jobs/scrape/merge.py)): scrape still keeps stale jobs in memory (panel users keep seeing assigned roles). The public site treats `closed_at` as gone: 410 + drop from the jobs sitemap.

Repo (SQL only here):

- `get_public_job_by_slug(slug)` — join company; includes closed rows
- `list_active_public_job_sitemap_entries()` — visa-positive, `closed_at` empty, slug present

---

## JSON-LD

Built in [`catalog/service.py`](../../relocation_jobs/catalog/service.py) `job_posting_json_ld` (no SQL). Injected in the first HTML response (`<script type="application/ld+json">`).

| Field | Source |
|-------|--------|
| `title` | `{title} at {company} (Visa Sponsorship)` |
| `description` | Sanitized HTML from `format_job_description` plus a Kuchup note |
| `identifier` | Kuchup + catalog `id` |
| `datePosted` | `fetched` / `last_seen` as `YYYY-MM-DD` |
| `validThrough` | `datePosted + 30 days` while open; `closed_at` when closed |
| `employmentType` | `FULL_TIME` (not scraped yet) |
| `hiringOrganization` | Kuchup, `sameAs` `https://kuchup.com`, `logo` `https://kuchup.com/logo.png` |
| `jobLocation.addressCountry` | ISO from country key (`uk`→`GB`, `germany`→`DE`, …) |
| `jobLocation.addressLocality` | Job `location` (first comma segment) or company `city` |
| `url` / `applyUrl` | `https://kuchup.com/jobs/<slug>` (Google uses `url`; `applyUrl` is the LinkedIn-oriented extra) |

`hiringOrganization.name = "Kuchup"` is deliberate so LinkedIn maps the posting to the company page. The real employer is in the title and description. Google Jobs may ignore or downrank a hiring org that is not the employer — LinkedIn wrapping is the distribution target. Ops notes: [seo-indexing.md](../operations/seo-indexing.md).

---

## Interstitial (conversion)

Template: [`web/templates/job_posting.html`](../../relocation_jobs/web/templates/job_posting.html) + [`static/job-posting.css`](../../relocation_jobs/static/job-posting.css) (design tokens, not the Next Header).

Do not send cold traffic to `/pricing` first.

- Header: title, employer, location, visa badge (only if `visa_sponsorship` is true)
- Body: sanitized description HTML
- Sticky CTA: **Track & prepare this application in Kuchup** → save/OAuth
- Secondary text link: **Continue to the official {employer} career page** → `/employer`
- Value prop: workspace + MCP; Free is 30 credits/month and 20 MCP writes/day

Save does **not** spend a credit (looking-to-apply is a free tracking action). Monetization is the existing Free wall: company slots, replacement-role credits, MCP daily quota — [entitlements-and-opportunities.md](entitlements-and-opportunities.md).

---

## HTTP map

Routes live in [`web/routes/job_pages.py`](../../relocation_jobs/web/routes/job_pages.py), registered from [`web/routes/__init__.py`](../../relocation_jobs/web/routes/__init__.py). Explicit `/jobs/<slug>` wins over the marketing catch-all `/<path:slug>` in [`web/server.py`](../../relocation_jobs/web/server.py).

`/logo.png` and the extra robots sitemap line are in `web/server.py`.

---

## Tests

| File | Covers |
|------|--------|
| [`tests/scrape/test_merge.py`](../../tests/scrape/test_merge.py) | `closed_at` set on stale, cleared on rescrape; slug preserved |
| [`tests/catalog/test_public_jobs.py`](../../tests/catalog/test_public_jobs.py) | Stable slug, collision suffix, persist closed, JSON-LD hiring org |
| [`tests/web/test_job_pages.py`](../../tests/web/test_job_pages.py) | 200 + JSON-LD, 404, 410, sitemap visa-only, OAuth `next`, save → workspace, employer 302 |
| [`tests/web/test_public_api.py`](../../tests/web/test_public_api.py) | robots lists both sitemaps; `/logo.png` |
| [`tests/helpers/route_manifest.py`](../../tests/helpers/route_manifest.py) | Job page routes in the panel route manifest |

---

## Code map

| Path | Role |
|------|------|
| [`catalog/schema.py`](../../relocation_jobs/catalog/schema.py) | `public_slug` / `closed_at` migration + visa backfill |
| [`catalog/repo.py`](../../relocation_jobs/catalog/repo.py) | Persist slug/closed; `get_public_job_by_slug`; jobs sitemap query |
| [`catalog/service.py`](../../relocation_jobs/catalog/service.py) | JSON-LD, ISO country, closed/public predicates, workspace path |
| [`core/slug.py`](../../relocation_jobs/core/slug.py) | `public_job_slug_base` |
| [`scrape/merge.py`](../../relocation_jobs/scrape/merge.py) | Stale → `closed_at`; rescrape clears it; keep `public_slug` |
| [`scrape/descriptions.py`](../../relocation_jobs/scrape/descriptions.py) | `format_job_description` for page body + JSON-LD HTML |

| [`web/server.py`](../../relocation_jobs/web/server.py) | `/logo.png`, robots second sitemap, Jinja `template_folder` |
| [`positions/service.py`](../../relocation_jobs/positions/service.py) | `set_job_looking_to_apply` on save |
| [`homepage/`](../../homepage/) | Marketing only (`output: "export"`). No `/jobs/[slug]` route. |

---

## What this is not

- Not a Next.js SSR/ISR app. The homepage remains a static export copied into Flask.
- Not Google Jobs-first. Mis-attributed `hiringOrganization` is a known trade-off.
- Not an auto-apply or ATS proxy. The secondary button is a tracked exit to the employer.
- Not a change to panel board privacy. `/panel`, `/apply`, `/company`, `/api/` stay `Disallow` in robots. Only visa-positive catalog rows get a public slug page.
